claims.text: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts use PGM nanoparticles supported on oxides such as alumina or unmodified ceria.
Pretreating a nanostructured CeO2-ZrO2 composite can generate oxygen vacancies in the support.
An oxygen-vacancy-rich CeO2-ZrO2 support strengthens metal-support interactions with PGM nanoparticles.
The engineered CeO2-ZrO2 support improves PGM dispersion.
The engineered CeO2-ZrO2 support anchors PGM nanoparticles more effectively.
Stronger metal-support interactions stabilize PGM nanoparticles against sintering.
Interactions between oxygen-vacancy sites and PGM nanoparticles improve oxygen-storage capacity.
Interactions between oxygen-vacancy sites and PGM nanoparticles improve redox cycling.
Improved dispersion and redox behavior increase the number of accessible catalytic active sites.
Stabilization of PGM nanoparticles against sintering slows catalyst deactivation.
The engineered support will increase catalytic activity under cyclic automotive exhaust conditions.
The engineered support will improve catalyst durability under cyclic automotive exhaust conditions.
The modified catalyst will exhibit higher turnover rates than a conventional alumina-supported catalyst under identical exhaust conditions.
The modified catalyst will retain activity longer than a conventional alumina-supported catalyst under identical exhaust conditions.
The engineered support will permit a reduction in PGM loading without sacrificing catalytic performance relative to a conventional catalyst with standard PGM loading.
The anticipated benefit depends on maintaining the support's oxygen-vacancy concentration during operation at approximately 700-900 °C under redox cycling.
High sulfur exposure may limit the benefits of the engineered support.
Operating temperatures far outside the stated range may limit the benefits of the engineered support.
